prompt_en: Create a photorealistic photograph of a vivid atompunk isotope orchard inside a decommissioned 1962 reactor greenhouse. Show one unmistakably adult woman, using the supplied portrait solely as appearance guidance for her long wavy dark hair, gently oval face, warm brown eyes, natural straight-to-softly-arched brows, and softly defined coral lips. She is a night-shift isotope horticulturist, calibrating a chrome seed-vault as cobalt-glass fruit pulses among waist-high hydroponic vines, with credible fingers pressing one Bakelite control. A compact analog robot simultaneously offers one glowing specimen in articulated tongs. Make the architecture, machinery, and work gear all unmistakably atomic-age: cream-and-turquoise enamel panels, analog radiation gauges, finned aluminum housings, orbiting-electron motifs, condensed glass growing tubes, her practical silver lamé coverall and clear acrylic dosimeter, plus a hanging bubble helmet. Layer the frame so chrome fruit rails sit in the foreground, her working hands and seed-vault occupy the midground, and enamel reactor arches recede behind her. Use a medium-wide three-quarter environmental frame at waist height on a 40 mm lens, keeping her face, both hands, dosimeter, seed-vault, robot, helmet, vines, and reactor hardware simultaneously legible. Let warm reactor fixtures and cobalt fruit glow cast one shared light across face, chrome, glass, and enamel, with believable reflections, condensation, material wear, and contact shadows. It should feel like a physically built 1960s science-magazine production still.
